races.name: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Tarriance
runners_data.note: OR 105 top weight returning off a 78-day break for Andrew Balding and Colin Keane; sole confirmed front-runner who can dictate entirely on his own terms, though his recent Goodwood form shows he does not always see it out at this trip and a STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence in this prominent role.
runners_data.comment: Tarriance showed useful form with a third three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine danger off a mark of 105 — though he returns after 78 days off and his two most recent efforts were disappointing.

runners_data.name: Align The Stars
runners_data.note: Won twice over 1m6f at Sandown and arrives as the most credible stayer in the field for Charlie Johnston and Daniel Muscutt; a deep hold-up type who needs the pace to be honest enough to make his late run count, and his Goodwood course form is limited.
runners_data.comment: Align The Stars won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, which counts in his favour; however, he carries 134 lb and ranks seventh of fourteen on our rating, suggesting he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Burdett Road
runners_data.note: James Owen's six-year-old apprentice-ridden by Mason Paetel, holds a win at this course and distance combination but his last six runs include a string of modest finishes; genuine hold-up operator who requires others to force a searching pace, and recent form does not inspire.
runners_data.comment: Burdett Road arrives 28 days fresh with a trainer firing at 36% in the last fortnight, and our rating of 111 marks him out as the one to beat from 14 runners; yet to win in recent starts, a third four starts back shows he retains ability, and he brings distance and going experience into the equation.

runners_data.name: Hopewell Rock
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for George Boughey on this lightly-raced four-year-old who has placed at 1m2f on Good ground and steps up significantly in trip; naturally prominent, suits tracking Tarriance closely, and the Moore/Boughey combination commands respect despite limited 1m6f evidence.
runners_data.comment: Hopewell Rock shaped well when third two starts back and second on a pair of occasions in recent starts, and his experience on today's going is a clear asset at 134 lb; the chief concern is that he has been winless in his last five and was well beaten on his most recent outing.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this David O'Meara six-year-old who placed at 1m2f on Good ground at Goodwood last time; sits prominently by nature and the step back up to 1m6f on similar going to his best form looks well-timed, though he has not won since his handicap mark climbed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though a second three starts back offers a glimmer of encouragement; returning after 46 days off carrying 132 lb, he has run over today's distance and going before, and our rating of 102 suggests he isn't without ability.

runners_data.name: Nesthorn
runners_data.note: George Baker's four-year-old has not finished better than fourth in five consecutive outings, all run over shorter trips at Goodwood on similar ground; natural hold-up runner whose pattern of finishing fourth or seventh is consistent but uninspiring, and the step to 1m6f is untested.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Nesthorn has at least run over today's going before and steps back out after 21 days, but a fourth last time out remains his only bright spot in a patchy recent sequence, and carrying 130 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Aeronautic
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's five-year-old has placed four times at Goodwood including a fourth at this trip; prominent runner with a tongue-tie on, and Dylan Browne McMonagle gives him strong jockey ammunition, though his OR has slipped and he has not won since dropping to handicap company.
runners_data.comment: Aeronautic arrives 46 days between runs and yet to win in his last five starts, though a third three starts back shows he can mix it at this level; carrying 130 lb off an official mark of 97 may test his resolve.

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old has shown consistent placed form at Goodwood wearing a hood, and Sean Levey keeps the ride; a naturally prominent type with decent course form on this ground, but he has not won in nine attempts at Goodwood and tends to find one or two too good.
runners_data.comment: Nightime Dancer has run over today's trip and going, shapes as a genuine threat from his recent fourth and second, and our rating of 105 marks him as one of the strongest profiles in the field; the concern is he's winless in his last five starts and must prove he can convert.

runners_data.name: Sing Us A Song
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett and James Doyle represent a powerful combination on this four-year-old who won over 1m4f on Soft ground and placed twice at 1m2f on Good; prominent by style, the step to 1m6f on Good to Firm is an open question but his figures at Goodwood suggest he handles the track.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden send out William Buick on a horse who has won three of his last five starts including twice at 1m4f on Good ground; his natural race position is prominent but the depth of prominent types in this field means he is unlikely to get that berth freely, which complicates his chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures and with a speed rating that leaves plenty to find, Valedictory is hard to fancy at the weights despite three wins in his last five starts; the trainer's 26% strike-rate and experience over today's trip and going are genuine positives, but he faces a stiff ask off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Too Soon
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman claims 3lb for the Gary and Josh Moore yard who have not sent out a winner in the last 16 days; his most recent win came over 1m2f on Soft and his Goodwood turf form on Good going has been poor, with the hold-up style relying on a genuine pace that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but that victory came 56 days ago, leaving fitness a query, and he ranks ninth of fourteen on our ratings. Has run over today's trip and going, though his form in the last five starts is patchy either side of that win.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: S Woods's four-year-old won over 1m6f on Good ground at Goodwood last season and returns just 14 days after his latest run; by nature a front-running or prominent type, he cannot count on getting that position in this field, and the redistribution to midfield significantly constrains his ability to reproduce that 2023 course-and-distance success.
runners_data.comment: Bahadur has managed just one win in his last six starts, finishing seventh most recently, and ranks eleventh of fourteen on our figures — hard to fancy at these weights. He does arrive fit on a 14-day turnaround and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Small Fry
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's second runner is partnered by Oisin Murphy and has shown stamina over extended trips including 2m4f; his true style is prominent-to-front and he has won at 1m6f, but competing for early position alongside several rivals of similar inclination means he is unlikely to lead as comfortably as his best efforts suggest he needs to.
runners_data.comment: Small Fry has back-to-back wins four and five starts ago, but three successive defeats since — including two ninths — make him hard to fancy, and he ranks last on our figures. Has run over today's trip and going, but that counts for little at present.

runners_data.name: Incensed
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett's five-year-old carries OR 91 and Kieran Shoemark's experience; placed at 1m2f and 1m4f at Goodwood on Good ground, he is a natural front-runner by record who has been pushed into a midfield mapping, and with the trainer winless from four runs in the last fortnight his chance depends heavily on a tactical race that never quite develops.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Incensed looks hard to fancy off 124 lb — though a third three starts back and a second four starts back show she can find the frame, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Tarriance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, and with no genuine rival to press him early, he is set to control the pace from the front at a tempo entirely of his choosing — likely honest but not truly searching given his lone hand. Behind him, Hopewell Road, Stressfree, Aeronautic, Nightime Dancer and Sing Us A Song are all natural prominent types who will jostle for the limited early positions directly behind Tarriance, creating a compressed and potentially restless mid-group rather than a strung-out field. Valedictory, Bahadur, Small Fry and Incensed are all genuine prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred berth and have been mapped to midfield, meaning the race will likely be run in a tight, tactical bunch through the middle stages before a genuine test of stamina and acceleration in the final quarter-mile. This shape — a controlled, single-paced gallop set by one horse — strongly favours horses who can track the pace from just off the leader, burst forward in the straight, and sustain that effort over the stiff Goodwood finish; deep closers relying on a true gallop are at a disadvantage because the pace is not guaranteed to be fast enough to string the field out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tarriance Controls, Track-and-Strike Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tarriance sets an unchallenged, even tempo and prominent trackers from positions two to four deliver their challenges approaching the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Tarriance's uncontested lead produces a steady, well-regulated gallop that leaves the field bunched close, and the horses sitting just behind him — Hopewell Rock, Sing Us A Song and Stressfree — arrive at the straight with energy in reserve to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tarriance's uncontested lead produces a truly slow early tempo that compresses the field completely, causing a sprint finish that allows the deepest closers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow gallop invites Align The Stars, Burdett Road and Nesthorn to produce sustained late runs down the Goodwood straight, capitalising on the bunched field running out of room ahead of them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Types Break Free
scenarios.trigger: If two or more of Valedictory, Bahadur or Small Fry push forward early to claim their natural prominent position rather than accepting a midfield berth.
scenarios.body: The act of jostling forward increases the overall pace, creating a more genuine gallop that suits horses with a prominent style and strong stamina, rewarding those who get their position despite the competitive early stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tarriance Front-Runs to Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Tarriance steals enough of a break that he is never seriously threatened and the field fails to coordinate a timely challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: With Ryan Moore's Hopewell Rock and others unable to quicken past a relaxed leader who has conserved energy throughout, Tarriance's class advantage at OR 105 combined with his fresh legs off a 78-day break proves decisive.

watchPoints.text: Tarriance — watch whether Colin Keane allows him to stride clear unchallenged early; if he builds a five-length lead by halfway the rest of the field may struggle to reel him in before Goodwood's straight runs out.

Valedictory, Bahadur and Small Fry — watch the first two furlongs for any of these three pushing forward to claim their preferred prominent berth, as any surge for position would significantly increase early tempo and change the race's entire complexion.

Hopewell Rock — Ryan Moore will likely position him directly behind Tarriance; watch whether he can quicken past the leader entering the straight, as his ability to do so makes him the single biggest threat to the front-runner's control.

Align The Stars — watch his position at the halfway mark; if he is within four lengths of the leaders at the turn he is live for the Muscutt late challenge, but if already detached he will struggle to close on a Goodwood straight that does not always reward deep closers in a slowly-run race.

Nightime Dancer — the hood effect is worth monitoring in the parade ring; if he travels smoothly in midfield with his hood on during the early stages Sean Levey may be able to produce him with a well-timed challenge rather than being swamped by the prominent cluster ahead of him.

races.name: Coral Glorious Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Al Aasy
runners_data.note: A genuine Group-level performer at Goodwood (two wins at the track over 12f), William Haggas in excellent form at T14, and this represents a slight step back in trip from recent wins — sits comfortably prominent and is well suited by fast ground with a solid sim-going record.
runners_data.comment: Al Aasy arrives here a winner last time out and second two starts back, boasting experience over today's trip and going; the chief concern is that ninth three starts back hints he can lose his form abruptly, and 129 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Enfjaar
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's six-year-old has consistent form at Goodwood over shorter (10f) but steps up in trip here; naturally a front-running or close-tracking type who will find himself racing further back than ideal given the density of pace in this field, and his sim-going figures are modest at 9/15.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last four starts, Enfjaar brings solid recent form and has run over today's going before, with a rating of 112 suggesting he holds strong claims; the main concern is that eighth last time out, which raises a question mark over his current peak fitness after 46 days off.

runners_data.name: Ghostwriter
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and architect of the race shape; Kevin Philippart De Foy's five-year-old has a style-fit note suggesting he is racing somewhat outside his optimal scenario, and recent form figures (including a last-of-12 at Goodwood) give pause, but his tactical role as lone leader gives him an undeniable positional advantage.
runners_data.comment: Returned from a 46-day break, Ghostwriter brings solid recent form — third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going — carrying 129 lb, yet to win in his last four starts, but our rating of 122 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's five-year-old has solid course form including a win over 10f at Goodwood, but his natural desire to race up with the pace will be frustrated by the number of rivals wanting the same ground — William Buick will have to make a decision early about whether to fight for position or settle for a deeper berth.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Involvement has been largely out of the weights in recent starts — third last time out but sixth two starts back, and just the one win in his last six. Has run over today's distance and going, and 28 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: King's Gambit
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer partners a horse whose best recent form came from patient hold-up rides (runner-up twice at shorter), and this 1m4f trip at Goodwood on fast ground stretches him — sim-going is strong at 12/15 but a tendency to finish out of the frame in Group company (6th, 7th, 9th, 9th in last four at Goodwood) is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, King's Gambit did show a second four starts back and a second five starts back, and with distance and going experience in his favour, he arrives fit on 28 days' rest — the worry is his three most recent efforts have been disappointing.

runners_data.name: Midak
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' four-year-old was out just 14 days ago and carries headgear; a hold-up horse by style but form figures of 4-6-9-4-4 at similar distances suggest a horse that fills places without winning, and a sim-going record of only 4/8 on fast ground is the weakest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Midak nonetheless shows consistent placement — three fourths in recent outings — and has experience over today's trip and conditions; carrying 129 lb won't help, though our rating of 110 suggests there's ability here worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Opportunity
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly-raced four-year-old arrives with genuine progressive form (three wins from last five including two at Goodwood over 12f), but as a natural prominent runner squeezed into a midfield map position, James Doyle will need to find a way through from further back than ideal — the ability is there but the tactical situation is compromised.
runners_data.comment: Opportunity arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, yet he carries 129 lb, rates below his official mark, and ranks sixth of eight — the weight and rating gap are the checks on his recent momentum.

runners_data.name: In My Teens
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's Irish raider won last time over 12f at Goodwood and has Oisin Murphy engaged, but carries headgear and a trainer who is 0/34 in the 14-day window; the 34-day gap since last run and a history of struggling over extreme trips (10th and 7th over 2m) suggests this shorter test over 12f here actually suits.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below her official mark on our figures and ranked seventh of eight, In My Teens is hard to fancy despite a lively recent record that includes two wins and two seconds in her last five starts. Has run over today's trip and returns after 34 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Ghostwriter is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pressure expected from any rival equally committed to making the pace, he should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at Goodwood. The field contains a heavy concentration of prominent-style horses — Opportunity, Enfjaar, and Involvement are all natural front-runners or close trackers who will be forced to race closer to midfield than they would prefer, creating positional friction early and potentially a more compressed bunch racing behind Ghostwriter rather than a cleanly strung-out field. Al Aasy and In My Teens are the most natural horses to track Ghostwriter from a genuine second or third position, while King's Gambit and Midak will be required to deliver their finishing efforts from the back of the pack. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a clean late run and proven ability to finish powerfully on fast ground, provided Ghostwriter sets a genuine enough tempo — but with a sole front-runner able to control fractions, the greatest risk is a falsely slow pace that turns this into a sprint finish benefiting the horse closest to the action.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ghostwriter Dictates, Hold-Up Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ghostwriter controls the pace unchallenged and sets honest fractions that stretch the field.
scenarios.body: Ghostwriter rolls along in front at a measured but genuine clip, leaving King's Gambit and Midak needing to produce sustained late runs from the rear while the bunch behind the leader jostles for position; the true closers who can travel smoothly into contention off the bend benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure, Front Held
scenarios.trigger: If Al Aasy or In My Teens push forward hard to sit tight on Ghostwriter's heels and inject genuine competition.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens earlier than Ghostwriter would like, making it a test of stamina and rewarding horses who travel smoothly in the first three positions and pick up off a true gallop; horses with a strong Goodwood record and proven class on fast ground at this trip come to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Ghostwriter idles and the field concertinas, turning the race into a furlong dash from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The compressed field negates the closers entirely, and the winner emerges from the prominent horses who can quicken sharply in a short space; redistributed prominent types like Opportunity and Involvement finally find the position they naturally want and can exploit their turn of foot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind, Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses scramble forward early and the pace becomes genuinely punishing throughout.
scenarios.body: The race degenerates into a stamina slog on quick ground, exposing horses who have been racing out of their comfort zone positionally; a horse with proven staying power at this trip on fast ground and a clean passage from midfield claims a tiring field late.

watchPoints.text: Ghostwriter's recent Goodwood form includes a last-of-12 finish at the track — if he fails to stride on early and assert, the entire premise of a controlled solo lead collapses and the race shape becomes chaotic.

Opportunity, Involvement, and Enfjaar are all natural prominent types who cannot all get the position they want — watch the first two furlongs for crowding and bumping as three horses compete for two places directly behind Ghostwriter.

Al Aasy's drop to 12f after recent wins over that trip at Goodwood is a positive, but nine-year-old legs at a fast pace on Good to Firm ground in late July mean any signs of laboured movement in preliminaries should be noted.

King's Gambit with Jamie Spencer is a combination that depends on a genuine pace being set — if Ghostwriter dawdles, Spencer will have no tempo to aim at and the hold-up shape becomes redundant, significantly reducing his chance.

In My Teens is trained by Gavin Cromwell who has no winners from 34 runners in the T14 window — stable form heading into this Group 3 should be cross-checked against any late market moves before the race.

races.name: Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Santorini Star
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with strong form at Goodwood (two wins), handles Good to Firm well (7 sim-going runs, 4 wins, 4 places), and Tom Marquand will look to track Danielle closely over a trip she stays well; 42 days off is not a concern for Haggas.|
runners_data.comment: Santorini Star has winning form at this level — a winner three starts back and again five starts back — and she handles today's distance and going, making her a genuine threat off an official mark of 111. The concern is a 42-day break and an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Consent
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's mare returned from 72 days off with a win last time and her best form is on softer surfaces (three SOF runs in recent hist), making Good to Firm a mild query; Luke Morris keeps it simple from a prominent pitch and she stays the trip convincingly.|
runners_data.comment: That winning record in recent starts is genuine, but she sits bottom of our rankings and her speed figure of 91 leaves plenty to find; a lengthy 72-day absence and that tame ninth last time out make her hard to fancy, despite having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Danielle
runners_data.note: The sole genuine pace-setter here, and John & Thady Gosden have her in cracking form (back-to-back wins), but her STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she will be racing more forward than she typically does — she is a versatile type who has won from different positions, so Buick dictating from the front is deliberate rather than forced.|
runners_data.comment: Danielle arrives here in the form of her life, winning back-to-back and bringing both distance and going experience to the table; the 70-day absence is the one query, but at 135 lb she remains the one to beat on these terms.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: In-form operator who was second here at Goodwood last time over 1m4f and won over 1m6f at Goodwood in 2024 — however, this seven-year-old is a naturally forward-going type who has been pushed into a midfield slot because the front is already spoken for; the STYLE_FIT discount tempers confidence even with McMonagle aboard.|
runners_data.comment: Goodie Two Shoes arrives on the back of a runner-up finish 24 days ago, and her record in recent starts — placed three times in her last five, including a win — marks her as a genuine danger; the main concern is whether 135 lb tests her stamina over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Little Dorrit
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has run five consecutive races at 12f at Goodwood without winning, and while she is well-held in terms of OR (96 vs the field), she is the only true hold-up runner; stepping up to 1m6f could unlock more, but a slow pace makes her task harder.|

runners_data.name: Waardah
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' mare has winning form at 1m6f on soft and was second in the Lillie Langtry here last year, but she is a front-running type by inclination who cannot realistically secure that role with Danielle present; the style compromise and the trainer's 0-from-8 in the last 14 days are two reasons for caution even with Callum Rodriguez.|
runners_data.comment: Waardah showed smart form with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and she lines up with distance and going experience under 135 lb; the 63-day absence is the one question mark against her.

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: The three-year-old filly, trained by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Ryan Moore, has winning form on Good ground at Goodwood and is lightly weighted at 125lbs, but she carries a hood for the first time and is a naturally prominent racer who cannot get close to the front in this shape; her inexperience at this trip (stepping up significantly) adds further uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Amelia Earhart has disappointed in her last two starts — fifth most recently and sixth two starts back — though she showed better form when winning on two occasions further back. Going experience is in her favour, but she looks up against it here on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Danielle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-strong field and, with William Buick in the saddle, she is expected to set a controlled, unhurried gallop over the 1m6f trip on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood. That lone-pace scenario creates a genuinely uncontested lead, meaning the fractions will be dictated entirely on Danielle's terms without any external pressure forcing a burn-up. The field contains considerably more prominent-racing types than can realistically all occupy that position — Goodie Two Shoes, Waardah and Amelia Earhart are natural front-runners or close-up racers who are mapped to midfield here precisely because Danielle has first claim on the front, leaving those three unable to express their natural style. This race shape — a single unhurried pace-setter, firm ground and a well-strung-out field — strongly favours horses that can sit close to the gallop and quicken from a prominent position, rather than those held up hoping for a sprint they may never get.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Danielle Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Danielle leads without pressure and Buick controls every gear change from the front.
scenarios.body: Danielle sets a metronomic pace that suits her stamina, arriving at the home turn with petrol to spare; any horse that has tracked her closely and conserved energy will then have the short Goodwood straight to make their move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Trackers Sprint Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one or two prominent types successfully shadow Danielle within a couple of lengths throughout.
scenarios.body: A compact, strongly-run final two furlongs develops as those who track Danielle off a steady clip have more left than the front-runner; Santorini Star or Consent, both effective prominent operators, are best placed to capitalise on this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Types Intrude
scenarios.trigger: If Goodie Two Shoes, Waardah or Amelia Earhart manage to push forward and claim a closer berth than the map suggests.
scenarios.body: A busier early dynamic develops as multiple naturally-forward horses jockey for position, fractionally lifting the tempo and making the race more of a test for Danielle's dominance; any of those three who successfully advances their position early gains a profile advantage but must overcome the style-fit discount.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a backmarker benefits from a strong finishing run.
scenarios.body: Little Dorrit is the only genuine hold-up runner and has consistently finished mid-pack without winning, making this a low-probability shape; a truly strong gallop that winds up the pace in the final half mile would be needed to bring her into play, which contradicts the expected controlled tempo.

watchPoints.text: Danielle — if Buick elects not to lead or is taken on early, the entire race map collapses and any pace-shape analysis becomes redundant; watch her in the stalls and the first furlong.|

Goodie Two Shoes and Waardah — both are natural front-runners who may instinctively push forward at the break, which could force a fractionally higher early tempo than expected and erode Danielle's advantage.|

Amelia Earhart — running in a hood for the first time; if the headgear produces an edgy or wayward early display, Ryan Moore may be forced to anchor her further back than even the redistributed map position suggests.|

Little Dorrit — watch whether Ray Dawson attempts to ride her any closer to the pace over 1m6f compared to her recent 1m4f efforts; any change in tactics over the longer trip would signal a deliberate trainer decision worth noting.|

Going verification — the official card says Good but all race-day sectional reports confirm Good to Firm; any horse with a significant soft-ground profile (Consent, Waardah) should be monitored for market drift as punters absorb the true surface condition.|

races.name: Coral Stewards' Cup (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Soldier's Tree
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with three consecutive thirds here at Goodwood over this exact 6f trip; OR 108 gives weight to hold but the lone front-running role in a 28-runner field is genuinely advantageous if the field obliges with a gap.
runners_data.comment: Soldier's Tree brings consistent recent form — third last time out and a winner five starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before; a trainer firing at 36% and our top rating of 119 from a 28-runner field make him the one to beat, despite the big 138 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: William Buick booked for a horse with an outstanding Goodwood record (3 wins from 13 runs here) and proven form over both 5f and 6f on this ground; headgear reported, strong platform as a genuine prominent type who should land in the front rank naturally.
runners_data.comment: Dubai Bling won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but his record in recent starts shows two unplaced efforts sandwiched around that success, making him hard to catch at his best; 137 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Northern Champion
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a 3lb age allowance and three wins from eight starts at Goodwood; OR 103 gives weight to a horse whose youth may be an asset, and Ashley Lewis (5) is a booking worth noting on a horse that acts well on this going.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and boasts experience over today's trip and going, but that ninth two starts back shows vulnerability, and carrying 135 lb from stall nine will test his resolve against stronger opposition.

runners_data.name: Mitbaahy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran who ran 2nd in this race at Goodwood over 6f, knows exactly what is required here; headgear worn, Jamie Spencer's hold-up/prominent blend suits a horse who handles this track without fuss.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in his last four starts — second last time out and a second four starts back — but yet to score in recent form, and a hefty 134 lb from stall 25 looks the chief obstacle for Mitbaahy, who has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: West Acre
runners_data.note: 183 days off the track is a significant concern for a horse returning from a long layoff, though three Goodwood wins show strong course affinity; headgear fitted, ran 3rd here in his last outing, and Darragh Keenan takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but consistent enough to demand respect, West Acre has distance and going experience to call on and our rating has him second-best in the field — the concern is 183 days off the track, and whether he returns sharp enough from that lengthy break.

runners_data.name: Sondad
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by nature — has won at Goodwood over this 6f trip — but the surplus of pace-setters means he is unlikely to get his preferred pitch and will race in a constrained position; his headgear is noted and his Goodwood course form is strong.
runners_data.comment: Sondad won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, but a mark of 98, carrying 134 lb from stall 21, and a patchy recent record that includes a ninth two starts back give pause.

runners_data.name: Run Boy Run
runners_data.note: Recent 4-day turnaround with visor in place; best form here at Goodwood tends to come at 5f rather than 6f, and a sequence of disappointing efforts (120040) tempers confidence despite a prominent style that might suit the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Run Boy Run has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going, but his last two outings have disappointed, and returning just four days later from stall 24 under 133 lb makes this a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Visor fitted for this one; most of his Goodwood form has come over 7f rather than 6f, and he has placed twice here at the longer trip — stepping back in distance is a question mark, though the prominent style is correct for the expected shape.
runners_data.comment: Two Tribes has run over today's trip and going, shaped with clear promise when runner-up last time out just seven days ago, and his rating of 109 ranks him among the leading contenders in a big field; the worry is that he's winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Get It
runners_data.note: 314 days off the track is a serious flag for an eight-year-old hold-up horse; his Goodwood form over 6f includes two wins but this lengthy absence makes confidence very difficult, and Pat Cosgrave partners a horse who clearly needs things to fall perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Get It won twice in his last five starts but has been unplaced in two of his three most recent outings, and 314 days off the track is a significant fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 132 lb from stall 27 adds further questions.

runners_data.name: Completely Random
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking sharpens interest in a horse that won a Goodwood 6f handicap on his last visit; ran 2nd here last time, though his recent form (110020) shows a dip from the peak, and headgear reported.
runners_data.comment: Completely Random arrives here fit from a run just seven days ago, has experience over today's trip and going, and his rating of 109 underlines his strong claims; the main risk is a disappointing unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Garfield Shadow
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse (3321/2) whose last five runs include three placed efforts at Goodwood — apprentice Harry Vigors (5) takes the ride but the horse's track record is solid and the prominent style fits the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 26 of 28 on our figures, Garfield Shadow faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 131 lb from stall 28, and his rating of 97 leaves him well held on paper — though he has experience over today's trip and going, returns on a fair 25-day break, and that recent win two starts back offers a crumb of hope.

runners_data.name: Tuco Salamanca
runners_data.note: Won his last start at Sandown and has winning form at Goodwood; however, his natural front-running preference means he is unlikely to secure that spot in this field and will be held up slightly against his instincts, which blunts his effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 24 of 28 on our figures and carrying 131 lb from stall 15, Tuco Salamanca is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last five starts — a winner last time out but a well-beaten sixth two starts back. Has run over today's trip and going, and the trainer is striking at 30%.

runners_data.name: Stratusnine
runners_data.note: Won last time at Goodwood over this trip — course form is highly relevant — but the surplus of prominent types forces him into a position he won't naturally hold; headgear not noted, Hugo Palmer has 4 from 29 in the past 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Stratusnine won last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, though his form in recent starts has been inconsistent — third and eighth in the two runs preceding that success — and 131 lb is a stiff burden to overcome again so quickly.

runners_data.name: Annaf
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with no wins from 15 starts in similar going conditions; finishing 7th, 3rd, 13th, 13th, 6th in recent Goodwood visits paints a picture of a horse who struggles to land a blow here despite racing at a track he visits frequently.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Annaf at least showed some spark when third two runs back, but a struggling trainer — just 1 from 28 recently — and 130 lb to carry are real negatives, even with distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Invictus Gold
runners_data.note: Headgear fitted; ran 3rd at Goodwood over 6f two runs ago and has placed on soft — this going is likely quicker than ideal, and Jason Watson rides a horse whose form (5-3928) is inconsistent.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Invictus Gold does bring distance and going experience to the table, and his second two starts back shows he can mix it at this level — but an eighth last time out and a nine-stone-four burden make the case far from straightforward.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Won this race at Goodwood over 6f a year ago — the course-and-distance form is directly relevant — but like several others he is a natural front-runner who will struggle to replicate his winning position in this field; Sean Levey takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner four starts back, Fandom arrives 21 days fresh with distance and going experience in his favour; a fourth two starts back and that unplaced effort three starts back temper expectations, though a rating of 102 suggests he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Far Above Dream
runners_data.note: Won four of his last five starts at Goodwood over 6f, an exceptional course record, and Kieran Shoemark has been in fine form; races up with the pace by nature but the crowded prominent berths mean he'll race off his ideal position, which is the primary reservation.
runners_data.comment: Far Above Dream has won three of his last five starts, but ranked 22nd of 28 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here. He has run over today's trip and going, a 42-day break gives pause, and draw 23 at least comes with a trainer firing at 36%.

runners_data.name: Hammer The Hammer
runners_data.note: Recent form of 056-00 is uninspiring and the OR of 99 with a 7lb apprentice (Toby Moore) does not inspire confidence; Goodwood record is moderate and Kevin Ryan has had no winners in the past 14 days from 22 runners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall 16, Hammer The Hammer at least brings distance and going experience to the table, though a trainer without a winner in 22 recent attempts is a significant concern heading into this.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Tom Marquand are a strong combination and the horse has two wins at Goodwood over 6f; 42 days since last run is not a concern for this stable, and headgear noted — the main issue is being pushed out of his natural front-end position.
runners_data.comment: Realign won two starts back but has finished eighth on his most recent outing, and 42 days off adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 128 lb from stall 18, and our rating of 103 suggests residual ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: Flash Harry
runners_data.note: Clive Cox has three from 27 in the past fortnight; the horse won a Goodwood 6f handicap in his recent form but has been off 42 days and the latest effort (0) is discouraging — Jack Nicholls (3) is an interesting apprentice booking on a horse whose best ground is Good.
runners_data.comment: Flash Harry showed he can win at this level — a winner four starts back and a third five starts back — but an unplaced latest effort and a sixth before that cast doubt on current form; he has experience of today's trip and going, and 128 lb is no light burden.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Whisper
runners_data.note: 77 days off the track and Oisin Murphy's booking raises the profile; no course wins at Goodwood but has placed at this track, and Andrew Balding has eight from 45 in the past fortnight — returning from a break at OR 97 with no prominent position available.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 77 days off, Berkshire Whisper is hard to fancy from stall 19 carrying 127 lb, ranked 21st of 28 on our figures — though he has run over today's distance and going, and a third three starts back offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Candy
runners_data.note: 4-day turnaround for Richard Spencer's third runner in this race; recent form of 416-00 is poor and the hold-up style relies on a late run that needs traffic to clear — Goodwood 6f wins earlier in career but current form does not inspire.
runners_data.comment: Candy has finished unplaced in each of his last two starts and ranks 23rd of 28 on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite a win four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and stall one is a neutral factor.

runners_data.name: Ferrous
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's runner has placed twice at Goodwood and is a genuine prominent racer at heart, but the race shape pushes him into midfield; his OR 99 and consistent mid-range form (426562) keep him competitive without suggesting a winning threat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ferrous nonetheless showed residual form with a runner-up finish last time out, 15 days ago, and he has experience of today's distance and going; carrying 127 lb from stall 12, he figures to run his race without necessarily threatening at the finish.

runners_data.name: King Of Light
runners_data.note: Won at Goodwood over 6f three runs ago and his OR of 91 gives him a lenient mark in this field; Marco Ghiani rides a horse whose natural style is prominent, but the crowded front end means he'll need fortune in running from a mid-division berth.
runners_data.comment: King Of Light has won in recent starts — a winner three starts back — but an unplaced run followed before finishing seventh last time out, and ranked 25 of 28 on our figures he looks very hard to fancy despite the fitness edge of a seven-day turnaround and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Excellent Goodwood record — four wins from 15 starts here including two at this 6f trip — and Jason Hart's booking suits a horse with real track specialist credentials; OR 93 with a low weight, though the race shape pushes him away from the front.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Dark Thirty faces a stiff ask here, but he does bring solid recent form — a winner two starts back and placed last time out — and has experience over today's trip and conditions. Fitness is fine at 14 days.

runners_data.name: Evening Saigon
runners_data.note: James Doyle pairs with a horse that has won at Goodwood over 6f and carries a headgear note; 42 days off the track and a recent form figure of 7 temper optimism, and his best efforts have come on softer surfaces than today's Good to Firm.
runners_data.comment: Evening Saigon was a winner three starts back and second two starts back, so he arrives with a solid recent profile, but a seventh last time out and 42 days off cloud his claims; experience over today's trip and going helps, yet 126 lb from stall 10 is no gimme.

runners_data.name: Gold Star Hero
runners_data.note: Has won at Sandown and Wolverhampton but Goodwood form is limited, with a 5th here on soft last time; Michael Bell has one from 20 in the past fortnight, headgear fitted — this horse thrives on a sounder surface but the course is unfamiliar.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and fifth last time out after a 56-day absence, Gold Star Hero is hard to fancy despite three wins in his last five starts; the trainer's current 5% strike rate adds little encouragement, though he has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has raced 15 times in similar going at Goodwood over 5f with one win — today's step up to 6f is a new test; Saffie Osborne rides, 4-day turnaround noted, and a horse whose best form comes at the minimum trip may find the extra furlong stretching.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our figures and drawn in stall 26, Toca Madera has managed just one win in his last six starts, and his recent sequence of a fourth and an unplaced run offers little encouragement, though he has experience over today's distance and going and returns just four days later.

races.paceDynamic: Soldier's Tree is the one confirmed front-runner and, with just a single pace-setter in a 28-runner field, the gallop is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching — a rhythm that rewards those able to travel close to the pace without burning excessive early energy. Dubai Bling, Northern Champion, Mitbaahy, West Acre, Completely Random and Garfield Shadow are all genuine prominent types who should secure positions just off Soldier's Tree, creating a compressed, settled lead group rather than a war for supremacy. The field is heavily loaded with natural front-runners and prominent racers — Ferrous, Far Above Dream, Fandom, Berkshire Whisper, Dark Thirty, Realign and others cannot all get their preferred pitch and will be shuffled into midfield against their nature, meaning hold-up horses Get It, Annaf, Candy and Toca Madera will be racing among a crowd of frustrated prominent types who are not true closers. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in the first wave behind Soldier's Tree, hold a good position through the race, and quicken from that platform in the final two furlongs — prominent-to-midfield types with Goodwood course form and class are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier's Tree sets a fair, uncontested pace and the first wave of genuine prominent runners travel comfortably in behind.
scenarios.body: The compact lead group rolls along at a sustainable tempo, denying the true hold-up horses a meaningful late surge, and those who have been racing in the first five or six find the most straightforward path to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier's Tree and the prominent group go too steady, creating a falsely slow early pace that compresses the field.
scenarios.body: A bunched sprint develops from halfway, negating positional advantages and allowing horses with a turn of foot from deeper to weave through; genuine hold-up horses who find daylight can finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier's Tree is allowed to stride clear uncontested and the large field causes enough trouble behind to prevent a clean pursuit.
scenarios.body: With no rival to press and 28 runners creating traffic and interference in behind, Soldier's Tree dictates every fraction and proves surprisingly hard to reel in through the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types create a scrappy, uneven pace pattern with surges mid-race as they fight for position.
scenarios.body: The race breaks into sections with a disjointed flow, and a horse with the tactical versatility and course craft to avoid the worst of the trouble picks its way through late; Goodwood specialists from mid-division benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Dubai Bling and Northern Champion are both genuine prominent types with strong Goodwood form who should land in the first wave naturally — watch whether they can travel into the first two or three without being crowded by the surplus of runners also seeking that position.

Soldier's Tree's ability to get a clear lead unchallenged is the pivot of this race — if another runner breaks sharply and challenges for the front, the whole pace dynamic shifts from settled to pressured, dramatically changing which profiles benefit.

Far Above Dream's exceptional Goodwood course record (4 wins from recent starts here over 6f) means Kieran Shoemark will be trying hard to recover a forward position even from the mapped midfield placement — watch his early stride out of the stalls.

races.name: Phase Eight Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wild Desert
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 3yo has strong Goodwood form over 7f including a course win, and Buick's ability to control tempo from the front is the race's defining tactical factor — though classed as Prominent, any drop in engagement from out-of-role racing could temper his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Wild Desert was second one start back but is held back by a sixth last time out and a rating of 97 against tougher rivals; he has run over today's distance and going before, and a trainer strike-rate of 35% keeps him in the mix from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Aqpan
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's hold-up operator has been off 70 days and his last two starts on similar ground were modest (7th, 8th), making the layoff and recent form a concern, though a 7f trip at Goodwood did yield a win at Sandown previously.
runners_data.comment: Aqpan's trainer is firing at 42% in the past fortnight, and he has experience over today's trip, carrying 129 lb from stall 6; the main concern is a run of three consecutive poor finishes since his last win, and 70 days off the track.

runners_data.name: We're Goosers
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's runner carries strong claims: two Goodwood wins including one over 7f, a prominent style that maps perfectly to tracking Wild Desert, and Oisin Murphy in the plate — the combination of course, trip and jockey is a clear positive.
runners_data.comment: We're Goosers won two of his last five starts and has experience of today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform to go well off 125 lb; a return to form after last time's unplaced effort would make him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: Won here at Goodwood over 7f on his most recent start and races from hold-up to midfield, giving him the profile of a horse who benefits if the tempo is lifted — the tongue-tie is noted, and six wins from ten runs on similar going underlines course-and-distance competence.
runners_data.comment: Utmost Good Faith won last time out, which catches the eye, but he ranks tenth of thirteen on our figures and his speed rating gives little confidence he can reproduce that at this level, with stall 11 and 123 lb adding to the queries.

runners_data.name: Ghost Mode
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo is prominent in style but arrives having finished 6th in his last five visits to Goodwood's 6f; stepping up to 7f for the first time at this venue could unlock more, and Rob Hornby gets the ride off a 23-day break.
runners_data.comment: Ghost Mode won five starts back and arrives on a 23-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going — a strong profile that supports his second-place ranking among the 13 runners. The concern is a run of three unplaced efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Egoli
runners_data.note: David Egan partners Ralph Beckett's runner who won here over 7f last time out; the hood is retained, the 14-day turnaround is sharp but Beckett runs horses fit, and sim-going form of 9/10 is extremely strong — a prominent profile suits this shape well.
runners_data.comment: Egoli bounced back to form with a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear danger here. The risk is whether he can back that up after a couple of disappointing efforts before it.

runners_data.name: Naval Light
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's runner has back-to-back wins including one over 7f at Goodwood and gets the 3lb claim of Jack Nicholls — running style naturally prominent, consistent place record at this venue, and the trip is proven.
runners_data.comment: Naval Light arrives in fine nick with back-to-back wins, though an eighth prior to those tempers expectations slightly; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 118 lb from stall 8, and our rating of 92 suggests he holds his own in this company.

runners_data.name: Ironwill
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's runner is a genuine front-runner by nature but the congestion of pace types forces him away from his preferred early berth — his two Goodwood wins and solid sim-going record of 6/7 are appealing, but racing in a position he wouldn't choose blunts his chief weapon.
runners_data.comment: Ironwill won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but he carries 117 lb from stall 10 and has been fifth twice in his last five starts, suggesting he finds life tougher in stronger company; our rating of 96 gives him an each-way squeak.

runners_data.name: Proud Nation
runners_data.note: Richard Fahey's hold-up horse has a fine Goodwood record including a win and two places over 7f, and the natural running style means he genuinely sits where the map places him — the apprentice booking of Fentiman is the one mild negative in an otherwise tidy profile.
runners_data.comment: Proud Nation has experience over today's trip and going, and his second last time out shows he can compete at this level — but his trainer's current 2% strike rate from 45 runners in the past fortnight is a significant negative to weigh against his claims.

runners_data.name: Startled
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes fields this natural pace-horse who has won twice over 7f at Goodwood, but with several rivals also wanting to race prominently, his forte — getting to the front and dictating — is unlikely to materialise cleanly; the 49-day absence adds a small fitness query.
runners_data.comment: Startled showed he's capable when winning back-to-back two and three starts back, but a seventh last time out after 49 days off is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 117 lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Marengo Storm
runners_data.note: Another Hughes runner, Marengo Storm has won over 7f at Goodwood and wears a hood, but like Startled he is a genuine prominent type who must race further back than suits — his 5121 recent form is eye-catching but the race shape is working against him.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Marengo Storm faces a stiff ask here, yet he does arrive in fair nick — a winner last time out, and a winner two starts before that, with distance and going experience in his favour from stall one.

runners_data.name: Start Me Up
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners Richard Spencer's hold-up horse who wears a hood and won over 7f at Goodwood on her penultimate run — three wins from nine runs, genuine style fit in the shape, and 21 days between runs is comfortable.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins one and two starts back give Start Me Up some recent profile, but a fourth last time out and a ranking of 11th of 13 on our figures make him hard to fancy at the weights here, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ay Up Duck
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's runner won over 6f at Goodwood nine days ago and is a natural pace type, but a 7f step-up on Good to Firm and the squeeze of pace horses all wanting the same ground makes it hard for Nicola Currie to get him into his rhythm — the quick turnaround is also worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Ay Up Duck has winning form in his recent starts — a winner last time out is eye-catching — but he ranks last on our figures among today's 13 runners, and his trainer is badly out of form at 1/28 over the past fortnight. Experience over today's trip and going offers little consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Desert is the one confirmed front-runner and, critically, faces no genuine rival for the lead — the field's other prominent types (Startled, Ironwill, Marengo Storm, Ay Up Duck) are all being squeezed out of their natural position by sheer weight of numbers, meaning Wild Desert can dictate alone at a pace entirely of William Buick's choosing on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood. That scenario — a solo leader controlling tempo — typically produces a steady-to-moderate early gallop over seven furlongs, compressing the race into the final two, and placing a premium on those tracking the leader rather than those furthest back. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can physically accommodate: Startled, Ironwill, Marengo Storm and Ay Up Duck are all natural pace-horses but are unlikely to secure prominent berths, meaning they race out of role and their effectiveness is compromised. The tactical verdict is clear: a solo leader controlling an honest but unhurried pace at Goodwood over 7f on Good to Firm ground overwhelmingly favours horses who can track in second or third and sprint from a close position — prominent-to-midfield closers who sit within two or three lengths of Wild Desert hold the dominant advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Desert dictates a moderate, uncontested gallop and the race ignites only in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Wild Desert settles beautifully in front with Buick dictating every yard, setting a pace that does not truly test the field until the Goodwood hill kicks in — horses tracking him within two lengths are perfectly placed to swoop. We're Goosers, Ghost Mode and Naval Light, all natural prominent types with strong Goodwood form at the trip, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hotpot, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types fight for position early, driving up the pace and leaving the field strung out.
scenarios.body: Despite being mapped to midfield by the pace squeeze, Startled and Marengo Storm may attempt to assert prominence, creating early friction and lifting the tempo materially — burning off those who overcommit. The resulting honest gallop releases the hold-up horses: Utmost Good Faith, who won here over 7f last time, and Proud Nation, sound each-way types in this shape, would be the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wild Desert Dictates And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Desert's uncontested lead allows Charlie Appleby's runner to get a walk in front and prove impossible to reel in.
scenarios.body: Buick, supreme at tempo management, could slow the race to a crawl over the first half-mile, ensuring Wild Desert's class advantage over a lowly OR-105 field is maximised without a gruelling test — a sprint finish from the front plays to his residual ability despite racing slightly out of role. With sim-going form of 4/5 at this course and track, his course profile cannot be dismissed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely strong pace develops and the race becomes a true stamina/finishing-speed test in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This depends on hold-up horses racing honestly in their natural position and the pace proving genuinely punishing — less probable given Wild Desert's likely solo control and the redistribution of several prominent types away from their preferred roles. Aqpan and Start Me Up, genuine hold-up operators, would be the ones to sift through if this shape materialises, though both carry question marks around current form.

watchPoints.text: Wild Desert — if William Buick glances around early and sees no challenger, expect him to deliberately slow the pace to a crawl through the first three furlongs, compressing the race and making it nearly impossible for hold-up horses to generate winning momentum.

Startled and Marengo Storm — both are genuine front-runners by nature and if either pushes for a prominent pitch in the opening furlong, a brief but damaging pace duel could compromise their own chances while inadvertently inflating the tempo and aiding true closers like Utmost Good Faith.

Egoli and Naval Light — both won last time out at this track over this trip and arrive in form with strong sim-going records; if either tracks Wild Desert in second or third they are ideally placed and should be monitored for market confidence in the hour before post.

We're Goosers — Oisin Murphy has a strong record in handicaps at Goodwood and the horse's two course wins give him a clear edge in track knowledge; watch whether Murphy slots in directly behind Wild Desert or opts for cover, as that positional choice will be telling.

Utmost Good Faith — six wins from ten on similar going is an unusually strong stat, and a return to 7f at Goodwood where he won last time positions him perfectly for the scenario where the race develops into a true test — check for any drifting in the market given the 31-day break.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rock Of Cashel
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who needs a strong pace to deliver; won at Goodwood over 7f on similar going 44 days ago (6th of 22 at the same venue more recently) and Jamie Spencer will bide his time, but the likely controlled gallop set by Crest Of Fire is the chief concern.
runners_data.comment: Rock Of Cashel landed a win two starts back but has been unplaced either side of it in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, and drops from stall one carrying 138 lb — a solid each-way profile on paper, though consistency remains the query.

runners_data.name: Alpha Crucis
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has been running in softer ground (SOF predominantly) and has just one placing from 15 runs on similar going — the step back to Good To Firm is a significant flag; Gary Moore's yard is 0/16 in the last 14 days and a 57-day absence compounds the worry.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Alpha Crucis nonetheless posted back-to-back second-place finishes earlier in this sequence and a rating of 97 underlines his strong claims from stall five; the worry is that three subsequent finishes of fifth, fifth and sixth suggest he may be just finding his level.

runners_data.name: Boyfriend
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old has 14 of 15 runs on Good To Firm or equivalent and has won and placed at Goodwood at this trip — Pat Dobbs rides a horse ideally suited by the likely controlled pace from just off the leader; T14 form of 12/59 suggests the stable is in excellent health.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back and third last time out, so recent form gives him solid claims, but 50 days off and a hefty 136 lb to carry from stall 12 are the checks on his chance; has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Real Gain
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes the ride on this six-year-old but he has been absent 86 days, his recent Goodwood form shows a 5th and 4th from 8f races, and a trainer strike rate of 0/10 in the 14-day window makes this hard to support off a long break.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Real Gain nonetheless showed a third five starts back and boasts experience over today's trip and going. Carrying 136 lb from stall 18 after an 86-day absence is worth monitoring, but a rating of 97 marks him out as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: El Matador
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old has been placed in four of five recent starts (2233) including two second-place finishes at Goodwood and Sandown; Hector Crouch's booking is a positive and the 10/10 sim-going record underlines this going suits — a horse drawn to run in the prominent zone who can sit close to the pace ideally.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and classy in recent starts, El Matador has finished third or better in four of his last five outings and shaped with plenty of promise; he has run over today's distance and going and our rating puts him right in the mix — though 135 lb and a 37-day absence are the main questions.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: James Owen's yard is in excellent form (18/50 T14) and Kieran Shoemark is retained; the visor is noted and the horse has placed in conditions like today, though most of that placed form has come over longer trips (10-12f) and the step down to 1m1f needs passing.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ammes does offer encouragement — a second three starts back and a third five starts back suggest he finds a way into contention, though converting that into success has eluded him; a trainer firing at 36% and a return after 28 days at least give connections reason for optimism.

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Has course form at Goodwood (3rd from 8f) and ran recently (21 days), but the last three runs show declining figures (8-3-6) and a soft-ground win over 7f at Stamford Bridge is the best effort — pace dynamics do not particularly favour this prominent type if shunted back in a crowded field.
runners_data.comment: Ran well for third two starts back but has been beaten out of the places at either end of that, including sixth last time out; has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is no gimme, though 21 days gives him a fair enough prep.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes, which is a critical concern in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace with a strong final-furlong emphasis; the hg:p (hood) is noted and Michael Appleby's 1/28 in 14 days is modest — best watched rather than backed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and carrying 134 lb from stall 7, Nostrum's most recent efforts have been modest — though a second four starts back hints at ability; the trainer's lean current spell (1/28) is an added concern, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sweet Reward
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's nine-year-old is a natural prominent racer with two recent wins at Goodwood at this trip, but with so many horses competing for prominent positions he is mapped to midfield, meaning his best form may be compromised by having to race out of his preferred slot; recent Goodwood course form (1-1-2) is nonetheless striking.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts show he can find the winner's enclosure, and he has run over today's trip and going before — but that ninth last time out and a ranking of 16th of 18 on our figures make him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Point Of Contact
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence is always significant but this four-year-old has been pushed back from his natural prominent position by sheer field density; his sole win came at 9f on Good ground and he has Goodwood course experience, but racing further back than ideal blunts his profile in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has been beaten into the mid-pack either side of it, and today's 134 lb burden doesn't help his cause; he has run over today's trip and going, though, and there's a small ratings edge to work with.

runners_data.name: Shafdar
runners_data.note: Won at Goodwood over 8f and has strong local course form (1W, 1P from 3 local runs); David Egan rides and the tie-back headgear is noted — a hold-up horse with a good record on similar ground who needs the pace to develop in his favour approaching the home turn.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, Shafdar is hard to fancy on recent form, though two wins in his last six starts shows ability is there; the 49-day absence adds a question mark, but he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Crest Of Fire
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and pace controller — Tom Marquand on a lightly-weighted 3-year-old who has won over 8f at Stamford Bridge and placed at Goodwood; no rival will fight for the lead, giving him a free hand, though he has yet to win at Goodwood itself and lacks the sim-going record of some rivals (7/9).
runners_data.comment: Crest Of Fire arrives here in solid heart — second last time out and third three starts back, with experience of today's trip and going — and at 132 lb he carries a hefty burden that could blunt his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Thinthread
runners_data.note: George Baker's four-year-old won over 10f at Stamford Bridge and placed over 10f at Hereford, so the 1m1f trip here is not a stretch — but he is a genuine prominent type who is unlikely to get his favoured position in this crowded field, and his sim-going record is absent from the data which is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the weights on our figures, Thinthread is hard to fancy at these weights despite a win three starts back and a third two starts back; he arrives reasonably fresh at 30 days, but his last two efforts have disappointed.

runners_data.name: Great Chieftain
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's five-year-old has 14 of 15 runs at Goodwood (5W, 7P) which is an outstanding course profile, and he ran just 17 days ago showing freshness; he wants to race prominently but this race's density means he may not secure that berth — his course familiarity remains the key selling point.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Great Chieftain at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and 17 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, carrying 131 lb from stall 11 makes life harder for a gelding who has struggled for consistency.

runners_data.name: First Ambition
runners_data.note: Michael Keady's five-year-old has never threatened in five starts over 8f at Stamford Bridge and Southwell (all 6th or worse) and the trainer is 0/8 in the 14-day window — a horse whose natural prominent style cannot be accommodated and whose form profile does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three sixths and a seventh among them, First Ambition faces a stiff task ranked 15 of 18 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and 30 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but the overall profile makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Blue Courvoisier
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old has an exceptional Goodwood record (2W, 4P from 6 runs on similar going) and is well-suited by Good To Firm; Saffie Osborne takes over from what looks a straightforward prominent draw, and at OR 91 she is effectively the most course-reliable horse in the field on this going.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has returned unplaced most recently, and 44 days off the track adds a fitness query; has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 96 suggests some unexposed ability, though he'll need to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Alcaraz
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse who has placed twice over 10f on soft and Good at Windsor — the step up in class at Goodwood at 1m1f is a query, and C Y Ho is not a top booking; a 72-day absence is the longest in the field and sim-going evidence (0W, 1P from 11) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13th of 18 on our figures, Alcaraz heads here 72 days fresh with a second three starts back as his recent highlight — but fifth and eighth in more recent outings make him hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Thunder Wonder
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has placed at 9f at Goodwood twice (3rd and 4th) on similar going and Marco Ghiani takes the ride; a genuine hold-up horse who ran 32 days ago, he needs a strong pace to deliver but has the Goodwood and going profile to be thereabouts if conditions suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Thunder Wonder faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out at least shows some recent spark.

races.paceDynamic: Crest Of Fire is the lone confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field on Good To Firm ground at Goodwood over 1m1f, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, Tom Marquand can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits a 3-year-old carrying just 132lbs. The pace will be controlled and sustainable rather than blistering — a steadily-run affair that compresses the field and makes a clean passage from behind harder to achieve late on. This field contains considerably more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Sweet Reward, Point Of Contact, Thinthread, Great Chieftain and First Ambition are all natural front-to-prominent racers who will be shuffled back into a midfield mass, further muddying the water for genuine hold-up horses trying to come from deep. The tactical verdict is clear: horses who can slot in just behind the pace — the true early-to-mid-race prominent brigade who do secure those slots, led by Boyfriend, El Matador and Blue Courvoisier — are best positioned to exploit a controlled pace on fast ground, while deep closers face a chaotic midfield to navigate without a strong gallop to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crest Of Fire Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Crest Of Fire is allowed to bowl along uncontested and the pace stays honest enough to stretch but not blow the field apart.
scenarios.body: Tom Marquand sits a comfortable lead through the first half, dictating fractions on Good To Firm ground that suit a front-runner with a clean sight of the rail; horses tracking the pace tightly have the best chance to pounce but few can get close enough cleanly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Crest Of Fire within two lengths makes a smooth move turning for home and powers clear before the hold-up horses can organise.
scenarios.body: The compressed pace suits a horse in the prominent zone with a high cruising speed and enough class to quicken under firm going; Boyfriend's Goodwood course form (1W, 6P, 14/15 sim-going runs) and El Matador's relentless placed form (2233) make them the natural beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than anticipated and Crest Of Fire sets a genuine gallop that strings the field out and leaves a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Rock Of Cashel or Thunder Wonder, both genuine hold-up types, would need a strong pace and a clear passage in the closing furlong — unlikely given the single front-runner profile and the midfield traffic created by the redistributed prominent horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Crest Of Fire fades from the front after setting too slow a tempo and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A flat-out sprint up the Goodwood straight from a bunch finish would theoretically help high-end speed, but with so many nominal prominent runners crammed into midfield the early-finishing horse from the right draw with the clearest run wins; Sweet Reward's recent sharp form and Point Of Contact's Oisin Murphy booking become relevant here, though both are racing out of their natural prominent slot.

watchPoints.text: Crest Of Fire and Tom Marquand control the pace entirely — if he is allowed to stride on unchallenged in the first two furlongs and build a 3-4 length lead, the race becomes his to lose.

The midfield is likely to be a traffic-heavy mass of redistributed prominent horses (Sweet Reward, Point Of Contact, Thinthread, Great Chieftain, First Ambition) who all want to race up with the pace — watch for bumping, checks and positional scrimmaging in the first half mile.

Blue Courvoisier's Goodwood course record (2W, 4P from 6 sim-going starts) is the most consistent in the field on this surface — if Saffie Osborne can slot her into second or third early, she becomes the most dangerous threat to Crest Of Fire.

Nostrum is flagged for fading in finishes and runs with a hood — if he appears to be travelling well into the straight but then weakens sharply, it will compress the field behind him and potentially block runners trying to come through on the inside rail.

Rock Of Cashel and Thunder Wonder are both genuine hold-up horses who need a genuinely run race — monitor early sectionals: if the pace looks slow through the first 3f, their chances recede significantly regardless of their going/course credentials.
